claim: BCR engagement with a TI-2 Ag but not with a T-cell-dependent (TD) Ag was able to induce the transcription of Aicda encoding activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID) and efficient class switching to IgG3 upon costimulation with IL-1 or IFN-α in mouse B cells.
source: Here, we report that B-cell receptor (BCR) engagement with a TI-2 Ag but not with a T-cell-dependent (TD) Ag was able to induce the transcription of Aicda encoding activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID) and efficient class switching to IgG3 upon costimulation with IL-1 or IFN-α in mouse B cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C-E demonstrating that NP-Ficoll (TI-2 Ag) but not NP-CGG (TD Ag) induced Aicda transcription and IgG3 production when combined with IL-1 or IFN-α.

claim: TI-2 Ags strongly induced the phosphorylation of protein kinase C (PKC)δ.
source: TI-2 Ags strongly induced the phosphorylation of protein kinase C (PKC)δ and PKCδ mediated the Aicda transcription through the induction of BATF, the key transcriptional regulator of Aicda.
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data in Figure 2A showing that NP-Ficoll induced stronger phosphorylation of PKCδ at Y311 compared to NP-CGG.

claim: PKCδ mediated the Aicda transcription through the induction of BATF, the key transcriptional regulator of Aicda.
source: TI-2 Ags strongly induced the phosphorylation of protein kinase C (PKC)δ and PKCδ mediated the Aicda transcription through the induction of BATF, the key transcriptional regulator of Aicda.
evidence: The claim is supported by data in Figure 5 showing that PKCδ-deficient cells had reduced BATF expression, and forced expression of BATF restored Aicda expression and IgG3 class switching.

claim: In PKCδ-deficient mice, production of IgG was intact against TD Ag but abrogated against typical TI-2 Ags as well as commensal bacteria.
source: In PKCδ-deficient mice, production of IgG was intact against TD Ag but abrogated against typical TI-2 Ags as well as commensal bacteria, and experimental disruption of the gut epithelial barrier resulted in fatal bacteremia.
evidence: The claim is supported by data in Figure 3 showing that PKCδ-deficient mice had severely reduced IgG production against NP-Ficoll and PPS3 (TI-2 Ags), but normal IgG production against NP-CGG (TD Ag), and Figure 6A showing reduced antibacterial IgG3.

claim: Experimental disruption of the gut epithelial barrier resulted in fatal bacteremia in PKCδ-deficient mice.
source: In PKCδ-deficient mice, production of IgG was intact against TD Ag but abrogated against typical TI-2 Ags as well as commensal bacteria, and experimental disruption of the gut epithelial barrier resulted in fatal bacteremia.
evidence: The claim is supported by data in Figure 6B-C showing increased bacterial CFU in blood and higher mortality in PKCδ-deficient mice after DSS treatment.

claim: NP-Ficoll induced little proliferation and no IgM production, whereas NP-CGG induced strong proliferation and IgM production.
source: Although NP-CGG induced little proliferation and no IgM production, NP-Ficoll induced strong proliferation and IgM production, whereas neither induced IgG production (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and B measuring proliferation and antibody production.

claim: Neither NP-CGG nor NP-Ficoll alone induced IgG production.
source: Although NP-CGG induced little proliferation and no IgM production, NP-Ficoll induced strong proliferation and IgM production, whereas neither induced IgG production (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 1B showing no IgG production with either antigen alone.

claim: NP-Ficoll induced IgG production, generation of IgG+ cells and Aicda transcription in the presence of TLR ligands.
source: Indeed, NP-Ficoll induced IgG production, generation of IgG+ cells and Aicda transcription in the presence of TLR ligands, LPS, R-848, or CpG, while NP-CGG did so marginally (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: NP-CGG induced IgG production, generation of IgG+ cells and Aicda transcription only marginally in the presence of TLR ligands.
source: Indeed, NP-Ficoll induced IgG production, generation of IgG+ cells and Aicda transcription in the presence of TLR ligands, LPS, R-848, or CpG, while NP-CGG did so marginally (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: IL-1α, IL-1β, and IFNα are efficient costimuli for IgG3 production in the presence of NP-Ficoll.
source: Since IgG3 is the most dominant class-switched Ig isotype produced in a TI-2 response, we screened various cytokines for their ability to promote the production of IgG3 in the presence of NP-Ficoll, and identified IL-1α, IL-1β, and IFNα as efficient costimuli for IgG3 production (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental screening data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and Figure 1C.

claim: NP-Ficoll was far more potent than NP-CGG for IgG3 production in the presence of IL-1α, IL-1β, or IFNα.
source: In the presence of these cytokines, NP-Ficoll was far more potent than NP-CGG for IgG3 production, IgG3+ cell generation, Sµ-Sγ3 CSR (detectable as the Iγ3-Cµ transcript from the switch circle DNA) (Xu et al., 2012; Kinoshita et al., 2001), and the induction of Aicda transcription (Figure 1C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C-E comparing NP-Ficoll and NP-CGG responses.

claim: NP-Ficoll or each of the cytokines (IL-1α, IL-1β, IFNα) alone could not induce IgG3 production, IgG3+ cell generation, CSR, or Aicda transcription.
source: NP-Ficoll or each of these cytokines alone could not induce those responses (Figure 1C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C-E.

claim: BCR signaling elicited by TI-2 Ag engagement is pivotal for the TI-2 B-cell response, namely induction of proliferation and antibody production, as well as potentiation of CSR to IgG.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that BCR signaling elicited by TI-2 Ag engagement is pivotal for the TI-2 B-cell response, namely induction of proliferation and antibody production, as well as potentiation of CSR to IgG.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation based on the experimental data presented in Figure 1.

claim: NP-Ficoll-induced phosphorylation of PKCδ tyrosine 311 (Y311) more strongly than NP-CGG.
source: By Western blot analyses for BCR signaling using NP-specific B cells, we noticed that NP-Ficoll-induced phosphorylation of PKCδ tyrosine 311 (Y311), indicative of activation of the kinase (Balasubramanian et al., 2006), more strongly than NP-CGG (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2A and cites a reference for the significance of Y311 phosphorylation.

claim: Phosphorylation of PKCδ tyrosine 311 (Y311) is indicative of activation of the kinase.
source: By Western blot analyses for BCR signaling using NP-specific B cells, we noticed that NP-Ficoll-induced phosphorylation of PKCδ tyrosine 311 (Y311), indicative of activation of the kinase (Balasubramanian et al., 2006), more strongly than NP-CGG (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Balasubramanian et al., 2006.

claim: PKCδ belongs to a novel PKC subfamily.
source: PKCδ belongs to a novel PKC subfamily (Salzer et al., 2016), whose function in the immune response remains elusive.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Salzer et al., 2016.

claim: The function of PKCδ in the immune response remains elusive.
source: PKCδ belongs to a novel PKC subfamily (Salzer et al., 2016), whose function in the immune response remains elusive.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field at the time of writing.

claim: B cells from Prkcd−/− mice normally proliferate and produce IgM when stimulated with NP-Ficoll alone.
source: B cells from Prkcd−/− mice normally proliferate and produce IgM when stimulated with NP-Ficoll alone (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: Upon costimulation with NP-Ficoll and IL-1α, IL-1β, or IFNα, Prkcd−/− B cells produced comparable levels of IgM but markedly reduced levels of IgG3 compared to Prkcd+/+ cells.
source: Upon costimulation with NP-Ficoll and IL-1α, IL-1β, and IFNα, Prkcd−/− B cells produced comparable levels of IgM but markedly reduced levels of IgG3 compared to Prkcd+/+ cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Class switching occurs along with cell division.
source: As class switching occurs along with cell division (Deenick et al., 1999), we analyzed the frequency of IgG3+ cells at each cell division using B cells labeled with CellTrace Violet (CTV).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Deenick et al., 1999.

claim: Cell division was almost equivalent between Prkcd+/+ and Prkcd−/− cells after costimulation with any of the cytokines and NP-Ficoll.
source: While cell division was almost equivalent between these cells after costimulation with any of the cytokines and NP-Ficoll (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), the frequencies of IgG3+ cells barely increased at any points of cell division in Prkcd−/− cells in contrast to Prkcd+/+ cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by CTV dilution data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The frequencies of IgG3+ cells barely increased at any points of cell division in Prkcd−/− cells in contrast to Prkcd+/+ cells.
source: While cell division was almost equivalent between these cells after costimulation with any of the cytokines and NP-Ficoll (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), the frequencies of IgG3+ cells barely increased at any points of cell division in Prkcd−/− cells in contrast to Prkcd+/+ cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: PKCδ is necessary for generation of IgG3+ cells regardless of cell division.
source: Therefore, PKCδ is necessary for generation of IgG3+ cells regardless of cell division.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing that PKCδ-deficient cells fail to generate IgG3+ cells despite normal cell division.

claim: Igh locus CSR to IgG3 assessed by the circle Iγ3-Cµ transcript and the expression of Aicda transcripts were attenuated in Prkcd−/− B cells.
source: Accordingly, Igh locus CSR to IgG3 assessed by the circle Iγ3-Cµ transcript and the expression of Aicda transcripts were attenuated in Prkcd−/− B cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: PKCδ mediates the expression of AID and class switching to IgG3 induced by BCR stimulation with TI-2 Ag and IL-1/IFNα costimulation.
source: Collectively, these results suggest that PKCδ mediates the expression of AID and class switching to IgG3 induced by BCR stimulation with TI-2 Ag and IL-1/IFNα costimulation.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the data presented in Figure 2.

claim: Prkcd−/− B cells exhibited defects in the production of IgG and Aicda transcripts, but normal IgM production, upon stimulation with NP-Ficoll and TLR ligands.
source: Prkcd−/− B cells also exhibited defects in the production of IgG and Aicda transcripts, but normal IgM production, upon stimulation with NP-Ficoll and TLR ligands (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D, E), but no defects in the production of IgM, IgG, and Aicda transcripts, upon stimulation with TLR ligands alone (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F, G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D, E.

claim: Prkcd−/− B cells showed no defects in the production of IgM, IgG, and Aicda transcripts upon stimulation with TLR ligands alone.
source: Prkcd−/− B cells also exhibited defects in the production of IgG and Aicda transcripts, but normal IgM production, upon stimulation with NP-Ficoll and TLR ligands (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D, E), but no defects in the production of IgM, IgG, and Aicda transcripts, upon stimulation with TLR ligands alone (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F, G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F, G.

claim: PKCδ appears to be selectively required for TI-2-Ag-mediated BCR signaling to potentiate CSR to produce IgG.
source: Together with the above results, PKCδ appears to be selectively required for TI-2-Ag-mediated BCR signaling to potentiate CSR to produce IgG.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the combined data showing PKCδ requirement for TI-2 but not TLR-mediated responses.

claim: The numbers of follicular and marginal zone B cells in spleens were comparable between Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f and Cd19cre/+ Prkcd+/+ mice.
source: The numbers of follicular and marginal zone B cells in spleens were comparable between these mice, whereas those of splenic and peritoneal B1 cell populations were slightly increased in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The numbers of splenic and peritoneal B1 cell populations were slightly increased in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice.
source: The numbers of follicular and marginal zone B cells in spleens were comparable between these mice, whereas those of splenic and peritoneal B1 cell populations were slightly increased in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: PKCδ is dispensable for the development of B cells.
source: Thus, PKCδ is dispensable for the development of B cells, as previously described (Mecklenbräuker et al., 2002; Miyamoto et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by the B cell development data and citations to previous studies.

claim: The production of serum anti-NP IgM was slightly enhanced in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice after NP-Ficoll immunization.
source: Although the production of serum anti-NP IgM was slightly enhanced in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice, that of anti-NP IgG3 was severely suppressed (Figure 3A), and so was that of anti-NP IgG1, IgG2b, and IgG2c (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The production of serum anti-NP IgG3 was severely suppressed in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice after NP-Ficoll immunization.
source: Although the production of serum anti-NP IgM was slightly enhanced in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice, that of anti-NP IgG3 was severely suppressed (Figure 3A), and so was that of anti-NP IgG1, IgG2b, and IgG2c (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The production of serum anti-NP IgG1, IgG2b, and IgG2c was severely suppressed in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice after NP-Ficoll immunization.
source: Although the production of serum anti-NP IgM was slightly enhanced in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice, that of anti-NP IgG3 was severely suppressed (Figure 3A), and so was that of anti-NP IgG1, IgG2b, and IgG2c (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The proportion and the number of IgG3- and IgG2b-producing PCs were severely decreased in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice compared to the control mice 1 week after NP-Ficoll immunization.
source: Among the NP-specific PCs, the proportion and the number of IgG3- and IgG2b-producing PCs were severely decreased in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice compared to the control mice, whereas the number of IgM+ PCs was comparable between the two groups (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The number of IgM+ PCs was comparable between Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f and control mice 1 week after NP-Ficoll immunization.
source: Among the NP-specific PCs, the proportion and the number of IgG3- and IgG2b-producing PCs were severely decreased in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice compared to the control mice, whereas the number of IgM+ PCs was comparable between the two groups (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: PKCδ is required for the generation of IgG+ PCs and the subsequent production of IgG in the TI-2 response.
source: Therefore, PKCδ is required for the generation of IgG+ PCs and the subsequent production of IgG in the TI-2 response.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the data showing reduced IgG+ PCs and IgG production in PKCδ-deficient mice.

claim: The capsular polysaccharides of Streptococcus pneumoniae, such as pneumococcal polysaccharide serotype 3 (PPS3), are classified as TI-2 Ags.
source: The capsular polysaccharides of Streptococcus pneumoniae, such as pneumococcal polysaccharide serotype 3 (PPS3), are also classified as TI-2 Ags, and immunization with PPS3 is known to induce an Ag-specific IgG3 response (McLay et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to McLay et al., 2002 and general knowledge about bacterial polysaccharides.

claim: Immunization with PPS3 is known to induce an Ag-specific IgG3 response.
source: The capsular polysaccharides of Streptococcus pneumoniae, such as pneumococcal polysaccharide serotype 3 (PPS3), are also classified as TI-2 Ags, and immunization with PPS3 is known to induce an Ag-specific IgG3 response (McLay et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to McLay et al., 2002.

claim: Early production of anti-PPS3 IgM was modestly enhanced in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice after PPS3 immunization.
source: Although early production of anti-PPS3 IgM was modestly enhanced in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice, production of anti-PPS3 IgG3 was ablated in these mice (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Production of anti-PPS3 IgG3 was ablated in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice after PPS3 immunization.
source: Although early production of anti-PPS3 IgM was modestly enhanced in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice, production of anti-PPS3 IgG3 was ablated in these mice (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: PKCδ appears to be generally required for IgG production in response to a variety of TI-2 Ags.
source: Thus, PKCδ appears to be generally required for IgG production in response to a variety of TI-2 Ags.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing PKCδ requirement for IgG production against both NP-Ficoll and PPS3.

claim: After immunization with NP-CGG, the production of anti-NP IgM was transiently enhanced in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice at 1 week.
source: After immunization with NP-CGG, the production of anti-NP IgM was transiently enhanced in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice at 1 week, whereas anti-NP IgG1 and IgG3 titers were normal in these mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Anti-NP IgG1 and IgG3 titers were normal in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice after immunization with NP-CGG.
source: After immunization with NP-CGG, the production of anti-NP IgM was transiently enhanced in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice at 1 week, whereas anti-NP IgG1 and IgG3 titers were normal in these mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: PKCδ signaling is required for IgG production in a TI-2 response, but not in a TD response.
source: These data indicated that PKCδ signaling is required for IgG production in a TI-2 response, but not in a TD response.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the differential requirement for PKCδ in TI-2 vs TD responses.

claim: About 30% of the splenic donor cells were IgG3+ in the mice transferred with control B cells 3 days after NP-Ficoll immunization.
source: About 30% of the splenic donor cells were IgG3+ in the mice transferred with control B cells, whereas only about 3% were IgG3+ in recipients of Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f B cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Only about 3% of splenic donor cells were IgG3+ in recipients of Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f B cells 3 days after NP-Ficoll immunization.
source: About 30% of the splenic donor cells were IgG3+ in the mice transferred with control B cells, whereas only about 3% were IgG3+ in recipients of Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f B cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: IgG3+ cells emerged at the second cell division and their frequency was increased as the cell division proceeded in the cells of control mice.
source: IgG3+ cells emerged at the second cell division and their frequency was increased as the cell division proceeded in the cells of control mice, whereas the frequency of IgG3+ cells was extremely low in the cells of Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice at any point of cell division (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The frequency of IgG3+ cells was extremely low in the cells of Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice at any point of cell division.
source: IgG3+ cells emerged at the second cell division and their frequency was increased as the cell division proceeded in the cells of control mice, whereas the frequency of IgG3+ cells was extremely low in the cells of Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice at any point of cell division (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: PKCδ mediates the generation of IgG3+ cells in a manner unrelated to cell division.
source: Thus, PKCδ mediates the generation of IgG3+ cells in a manner unrelated to cell division.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing that PKCδ-deficient cells fail to generate IgG3+ cells despite normal cell division.

claim: The amounts of the Iγ3-Cµ circle transcripts and the Iµ-Cγ3 early postswitch transcripts were far less in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f B cells compared to control cells in vivo.
source: The amounts of the Iγ3-Cµ circle transcripts and the Iµ-Cγ3 early postswitch transcripts were far less in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f B cells compared to control cells, indicating fewer CSR events in the former in vivo (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The expression of Iµ-Cµ and Iγ3-Cγ3 germline transcripts was comparable between the Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f B cells and the control cells.
source: The expression of Iµ-Cµ and Iγ3-Cγ3 germline transcripts was comparable between the Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f B cells and the control cells, whereas the expression of Aicda was substantially reduced in the former (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The expression of Aicda was substantially reduced in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f B cells compared to control cells in vivo.
source: The expression of Iµ-Cµ and Iγ3-Cγ3 germline transcripts was comparable between the Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f B cells and the control cells, whereas the expression of Aicda was substantially reduced in the former (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: PKCδ mediates CSR to IgG3 through upregulation of AID mRNA, but not through the activation of Ig gene S regions in B cells responding to TI-2 Ags in vivo.
source: These results indicate that PKCδ mediates CSR to IgG3 through upregulation of AID mRNA, but not through the activation of Ig gene S regions in B cells responding to TI-2 Ags in vivo.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the data showing reduced AID expression but normal germline transcripts in PKCδ-deficient cells.

claim: The reconstitution of AID expression restored IgG3 class switching to a frequency comparable to the same cells reconstituted with PKCδ.
source: The reconstitution of AID expression restored IgG3 class switching to a frequency comparable to the same cells reconstituted with PKCδ (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: PKCδ mediates class switching to IgG3 by upregulating the expression of AID in the TI-2 response.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that PKCδ mediates class switching to IgG3 by upregulating the expression of AID in the TI-2 response.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the rescue experiments showing that AID reconstitution restores class switching in PKCδ-deficient cells.

claim: Expression of Aicda gene is regulated by various transcriptional factors.
source: It has been shown that expression of Aicda gene is regulated by various transcriptional factors (Vaidyanathan et al., 2014; Tran et al., 2010; Crouch et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The amount of Batf mRNA was markedly lower in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f B cells than in control cells collected from mice immunized with NP-Ficoll.
source: Among the genes tested, we found that the amount of Batf mRNA was markedly lower in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f B cells than in control cells (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The expression of BATF mRNA and protein was induced by in vitro stimulation with NP-Ficoll alone in PKCδ-sufficient B cells, but only marginally in PKCδ-deficient B cells.
source: The expression of BATF mRNA and protein was induced by in vitro stimulation with NP-Ficoll alone in PKCδ-sufficient B cells, but only marginally in PKCδ-deficient B cells (Figure 5B and C), whereas BATF expression was not induced by NP-CGG (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: BATF expression was not induced by NP-CGG.
source: The expression of BATF mRNA and protein was induced by in vitro stimulation with NP-Ficoll alone in PKCδ-sufficient B cells, but only marginally in PKCδ-deficient B cells (Figure 5B and C), whereas BATF expression was not induced by NP-CGG (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: IL-1α, IL-1β, or IFNα did not augment the phosphorylation of PKCδ.
source: IL-1α, IL-1β, or IFNα did not augment the phosphorylation of PKCδ nor induce Batf expression nor enhance the NP-Ficoll-induced Batf expression (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B-D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B-D.

claim: IL-1α, IL-1β, or IFNα did not induce Batf expression.
source: IL-1α, IL-1β, or IFNα did not augment the phosphorylation of PKCδ nor induce Batf expression nor enhance the NP-Ficoll-induced Batf expression (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B-D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: IL-1α, IL-1β, or IFNα did not enhance the NP-Ficoll-induced Batf expression.
source: IL-1α, IL-1β, or IFNα did not augment the phosphorylation of PKCδ nor induce Batf expression nor enhance the NP-Ficoll-induced Batf expression (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B-D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: PKCδ induces the expression of BATF downstream of the BCR in the TI-2 response.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that PKCδ induces the expression of BATF downstream of the BCR in the TI-2 response.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the data showing that NP-Ficoll induces BATF in a PKCδ-dependent manner.

claim: BATF binds to a regulatory region of the Aicda gene to directly promote its expression.
source: It was reported that BATF binds to a regulatory region of the Aicda gene to directly promote its expression and that IgG3 production against TNP-Ficoll was impaired in Batf−/− mice (Ise et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Ise et al., 2011.

claim: IgG3 production against TNP-Ficoll was impaired in Batf−/− mice.
source: It was reported that BATF binds to a regulatory region of the Aicda gene to directly promote its expression and that IgG3 production against TNP-Ficoll was impaired in Batf−/− mice (Ise et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Ise et al., 2011.

claim: Both the expression of Aicda and the frequency of IgG3+ cells were significantly decreased in BATF knockdown cells compared with the mock-transduced control cells.
source: Both the expression of Aicda and the frequency of IgG3+ cells were significantly decreased in BATF knockdown cells compared with the mock-transduced control cells (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5D and E.

claim: Forced expression of BATF in B1-8hi Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f B cells partially but significantly restored Aicda expression and the generation of IgG3+ cells in the recipient mice immunized with NP-Ficoll.
source: Conversely, forced expression of BATF in B1-8hi Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f B cells partially but significantly restored Aicda expression and the generation of IgG3+ cells in the recipient mice immunized with NP-Ficoll (Figure 5F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5F and G.

claim: PKCδ mediates expression of AID and class switching to IgG3 through upregulation of BATF expression in B cells undergoing a TI-2 response.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that PKCδ mediates expression of AID and class switching to IgG3 through upregulation of BATF expression in B cells undergoing a TI-2 response.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the data showing that PKCδ induces BATF, which in turn induces AID and class switching.

claim: Commensal microbes induce an IgG response and confer protection against systemic bacterial infection.
source: Recent works have revealed that commensal microbes induce an IgG response and confer protection against systemic bacterial infection (Zeng et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Zeng et al., 2016.

claim: Among antibacterial IgG, IgG3 is most abundant and produced in a TI manner.
source: Among antibacterial IgG, IgG3 is most abundant and produced in a TI manner (Ansaldo et al., 2019; Koch et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ansaldo et al., 2019 and Koch et al., 2016.

claim: Production of serum antibacterial IgM, IgG1, and IgG2b was not changed significantly in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice.
source: Production of serum antibacterial IgM, IgG1, and IgG2b was not changed significantly, but that of IgG3 was severely impaired in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Production of serum antibacterial IgG3 was severely impaired in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice.
source: Production of serum antibacterial IgM, IgG1, and IgG2b was not changed significantly, but that of IgG3 was severely impaired in Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Antibacterial IgG2c was undetectable in both Cd19cre/+ Prkcd+/+ and Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mouse groups.
source: Antibacterial IgG2c was undetectable in both mouse groups (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text but data is not shown.

claim: The PKCδ-independent production of antibacterial IgG1 and IgG2b may be attributable to TD responses.

evidence: This is an inference based on the differential requirement for PKCδ in TI-2 vs TD responses and citation to Ansaldo et al., 2019.

claim: Antibacterial IgG3 is mainly produced by the TI-2 response.
source: Given that PKCδ was required for production of all IgG subclasses in the anti-NP TI-2 response (Figure 3), the PKCδ-independent production of antibacterial IgG1 and IgG2b may be attributable to TD responses, as reported for IgG1 (Ansaldo et al., 2019), while antibacterial IgG3 is mainly produced by the TI-2 response.
evidence: This is an inference based on the PKCδ-dependence of antibacterial IgG3 production.

claim: Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice exhibited increased numbers of aerobic and anaerobic bacteria in the blood compared to control mice after DSS treatment.

claim: The mortality of Cd19cre/+ Prkcdff/f mice was significantly higher than that of control mice after DSS treatment.

claim: IgG3 production by a TI-2 response via PKCδ prevents lethal bacteremia.

claim: Proximal BCR signal molecules such as BLNK or Btk are necessary for B-cell activation and subsequent IgM and IgG production in the TI-2 response in mice.

claim: BCR stimulation with a TI-2 Ag (NP-Ficoll), but not a TD Ag (NP-CGG), promoted transcription of Aicda and induced IgG3 CSR in the presence of a secondary stimulation.

evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings presented in the Results section.

claim: BCR engagement with a TI-2 Ag induced the phosphorylation of PKCδ.
source: BCR engagement with a TI-2 Ag induced the phosphorylation of PKCδ and PKCδ was required for upregulation of BATF expression, thereby mediated the induction of Aicda transcription and subsequent CSR to the IgG subclasses (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings presented in the Results section.

claim: PKCδ was required for upregulation of BATF expression.
source: BCR engagement with a TI-2 Ag induced the phosphorylation of PKCδ and PKCδ was required for upregulation of BATF expression, thereby mediated the induction of Aicda transcription and subsequent CSR to the IgG subclasses (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings presented in the Results section.

claim: PKCδ mediated the induction of Aicda transcription and subsequent CSR to the IgG subclasses.
source: BCR engagement with a TI-2 Ag induced the phosphorylation of PKCδ and PKCδ was required for upregulation of BATF expression, thereby mediated the induction of Aicda transcription and subsequent CSR to the IgG subclasses (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings presented in the Results section.

claim: PKCδ was dispensable for TI-2 Ag-mediated B-cell proliferation.

claim: PKCδ was dispensable for TI-2 Ag-mediated IgM production.

claim: PKCδ was dispensable for B-cell development.
source: By contrast, PKCδ was dispensable for TI-2 Ag-mediated B-cell proliferation, IgM production, as well as for B-cell development and the TD response.

claim: PKCδ was dispensable for the TD response.
source: By contrast, PKCδ was dispensable for TI-2 Ag-mediated B-cell proliferation, IgM production, as well as for B-cell development and the TD response.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings presented in the Results section.

claim: This is the first report of a BCR signaling molecule that is selectively required for CSR in the TI-2 response.
source: Thus, we have found for the first time, as far as we know, a BCR signaling molecule that is selectively required for CSR in the TI-2 response.

claim: TI-2 Ags such as NP-Ficoll can induce antibody response in the absence of major histocompatibility complex class II-restricted T cell help or MyD88-mediated TLR receptor signaling.
source: TI-2 Ags such as NP-Ficoll can induce antibody response in the absence of major histocompatibility complex class II-restricted T cell help or MyD88-mediated TLR receptor signaling (Gavin et al., 2006; Hou et al., 2011).

claim: NP-Ficoll, but not NP-CGG, was able to activate NP-specific naive B cells to induce proliferation, antibody production, and potentiation for CSR in vitro.
source: We demonstrated that NP-Ficoll, but not NP-CGG, was able to activate NP-specific naive B cells to induce proliferation, antibody production, and potentiation for CSR in vitro.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings presented in the Results section.

claim: Despite sharing the same antigenic epitope (NP) at a similar average number per molecule, NP-Ficoll and NP-CGG appear to elicit disparate BCR signal transduction.
source: Thus, despite sharing the same antigenic epitope (NP) at a similar average number per molecule, these Ags appear to elicit disparate BCR signal transduction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential responses to NP-Ficoll and NP-CGG.

claim: After Ag binding, the BCR is clustered and recruited to lipid microdomains, in which signaling proteins are localized that trigger B-cell activation signaling.
source: After Ag binding, the BCR is clustered and recruited to lipid microdomains, in which signaling proteins are localized that trigger B-cell activation signaling (Niiro and Clark, 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Niiro and Clark, 2002.

claim: Ag structure probably affects BCR dynamics or membrane organization of signal components.
source: Ag structure probably affects such BCR dynamics or membrane organization of signal components.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed differences in BCR signaling between TI-2 and TD antigens.

claim: A high-valency TI-2 Ag induces the formation of large BCR clusters in the lipid microdomains.
source: Consistently, it was previously reported that a high-valency TI-2 Ag induces the formation of large BCR clusters in the lipid microdomains (Puffer et al., 2007).

claim: PKCδ is known to control Ag-induced tolerance in immature B cells.

claim: A possible alteration of the mature B-cell repertoire in PKCδ-deficient mice is not attributable to the defective class switching to IgG3.
source: However, a possible alteration of the mature B-cell repertoire in PKCδ-deficient mice is not attributable to the defective class switching to IgG3, since the defect was obvious in the NP-Ficoll response by PKCδ-deficient, B1-8VH-knock-in B cells with a monoclonal anti-NP repertoire.

claim: Various transcription factors have been reported to cooperatively induce the transcription of AID in the TD response.

claim: PKCδ signaling might regulate other transcription factors in addition to BATF to fully upregulate the expression of AID to induce CSR in the TI-2 response.
source: Although we have not assessed the contribution of other transcription factors in the TI-2 response, since the expression of other candidate genes was intact in PKCδ-deficient B cells (Figure 5A), PKCδ signaling might regulate other transcription factors in addition to BATF to fully upregulate the expression of AID to induce CSR in the TI-2 response.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the partial rescue of AID expression by BATF reconstitution.

claim: PKCδ contains several phosphorylation sites, whose phosphorylation pattern affects its enzymatic activity and possibly the selection of downstream targets.

claim: Phosphorylation of Thr 505 and Ser 647 of PKCδ is known to be important for its enzymatic activity.
source: Although the phosphorylation of Thr 505 and Ser 647 of PKCδ is known to be important for its enzymatic activity, phosphorylation of these sites was constitutive in unstimulated naive B cells and did not increase after NP-Ficoll stimulation (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge and the authors' unpublished observations.

claim: Phosphorylation of Thr 505 and Ser 647 of PKCδ was constitutive in unstimulated naive B cells and did not increase after NP-Ficoll stimulation.
source: Although the phosphorylation of Thr 505 and Ser 647 of PKCδ is known to be important for its enzymatic activity, phosphorylation of these sites was constitutive in unstimulated naive B cells and did not increase after NP-Ficoll stimulation (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' unpublished observations.

claim: PKCδ exerts proapoptotic activity in peripheral B cells through nuclear translocation, unless BAFF signaling reverses it.
source: This observation and a previous report that PKCδ exerts proapoptotic activity in peripheral B cells through nuclear translocation, unless BAFF signaling reverses it (Mecklenbräuker et al., 2004), indicate a constitutive PKCδ activity in B cells irrespective of Ag stimulation.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Mecklenbräuker et al., 2004.

claim: There is a constitutive PKCδ activity in B cells irrespective of Ag stimulation.
source: This observation and a previous report that PKCδ exerts proapoptotic activity in peripheral B cells through nuclear translocation, unless BAFF signaling reverses it (Mecklenbräuker et al., 2004), indicate a constitutive PKCδ activity in B cells irrespective of Ag stimulation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the constitutive phosphorylation of PKCδ and previous reports.

claim: Augmented IgM production after immunization with TI-2 as well as TD Ags in PKCδ-deficient mice may reflect the lack of the general proapoptotic function of PKCδ.
source: Augmented IgM production after immunization with TI-2 as well as TD Ags in PKCδ-deficient mice (Figure 3A and D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) may reflect the lack of the general proapoptotic function of PKCδ.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed increase in IgM production and the known proapoptotic function of PKCδ.

claim: Phosphorylation of PKCδ at Tyr 311 is known to alter its intracellular localization and the substrate specificity.
source: On the other hand, phosphorylation of PKCδ at Tyr 311, shown here to be selectively augmented by TI-2 Ag stimulation, is known to alter its intracellular localization and the substrate specificity (Rybin et al., 2004; Steinberg, 2004) and to be involved in various cellular responses (Balasubramanian et al., 2006; Nakashima et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Rybin et al., 2004 and Steinberg, 2004.

claim: Phosphorylation of PKCδ at Tyr 311 is involved in various cellular responses.
source: On the other hand, phosphorylation of PKCδ at Tyr 311, shown here to be selectively augmented by TI-2 Ag stimulation, is known to alter its intracellular localization and the substrate specificity (Rybin et al., 2004; Steinberg, 2004) and to be involved in various cellular responses (Balasubramanian et al., 2006; Nakashima et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Balasubramanian et al., 2006 and Nakashima et al., 2008.

claim: To understand the mechanism of TI-2 Ag-specific BCR signaling that induces the expression of BATF and AID, it would be necessary to identify a specific substrate of the phosphorylated PKCδ at Tyr 311.
source: Thus, to understand the mechanism of TI-2 Ag-specific BCR signaling that induces the expression of BATF and AID, it would be necessary to identify a specific substrate of the phosphorylated PKCδ at Tyr 311.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research directions based on the current findings.

claim: PKCδ was not required for IgG production in the TD response, like other proximal BCR molecules.
source: In contrast to TI-2 response, PKCδ was not required for IgG production in the TD response, like other proximal BCR molecules (Khan et al., 1995; Xu et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data and citations to previous studies.

claim: In vitro stimulation with a TD Ag alone induced only a marginal level of phosphorylation of PKCδ and other signaling molecules.
source: In vitro stimulation with a TD Ag alone induced only a marginal level of phosphorylation of PKCδ and other signaling molecules (Figure 2A and data not shown) and did not induce proliferation, IgM production, and the expression of BATF.
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2A and unpublished observations.

claim: In vitro stimulation with a TD Ag alone did not induce proliferation, IgM production, and the expression of BATF.
source: In vitro stimulation with a TD Ag alone induced only a marginal level of phosphorylation of PKCδ and other signaling molecules (Figure 2A and data not shown) and did not induce proliferation, IgM production, and the expression of BATF.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the Results section.

claim: The TD Ag-mediated BCR signaling cannot exceed an activation threshold to induce gene expression leading to functional B-cell response including class switching.

evidence: This is a speculation based on the known role of CD40L in TD responses.

source: In the context of TD response, the recruitment of NF-κB and STAT6 to the 5′ upstream enhancer region of Aicda locus, in addition to BATF recruitment to the 3′ downstream region, is required for the transcription of Aicda (Tran et al., 2010; Vaidyanathan et al., 2014).

claim: Costimulation by IL-1α/β, IFNα, or TLR ligands may signal the recruitment of transcription factors to the 5′ upstream enhancer region of Aicda.
source: Since the in vitro stimulation by TI-2 Ag induced the expression of BATF but not of Aicda without the additional stimulation, such costimulation may signal the recruitment of transcription factors to the 5′ upstream enhancer region.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the requirement for costimulation to induce Aicda expression.

claim: IL-1 and IFNα induce the transcription of Aicda through activation of NF-κB in hepatocytes during hepatitis B virus infection.

claim: IgG production upon immunization with NP-Ficoll was dampened in IL-1α/β double-deficient mice.

claim: IgG2c production with NP-Ficoll plus poly(I:C) was dependent on the IFNα receptor on B cells.
source: Consistent with our in vitro data, previous reports showed the contribution of IL-1α/β, IFNα, and TLR ligands in several types of TI-2 responses: IgG production upon immunization with NP-Ficoll was dampened in IL-1α/β double-deficient mice (Nakae et al., 2001), and IgG2c production with NP-Ficoll plus poly(I:C) was dependent on the IFNα receptor on B cells (Swanson et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Swanson et al., 2010.

claim: IgG production against NP-Ficoll did not require MyD88-mediated TLR signaling.
source: While IgG production against NP-Ficoll did not require MyD88-mediated TLR signaling (Gavin et al., 2006; Hou et al., 2011), IgG production against pneumococcal polysaccharides requires TLR signaling (Sen et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gavin et al., 2006 and Hou et al., 2011.

claim: IgG production against pneumococcal polysaccharides requires TLR signaling.

claim: PKCδ seems to be needed for protection from pneumococcal infection.

claim: Some commensal bacteria express TI-2 Ag-like repetitive structures that elicit IgG3 production.
source: As commensal bacteria have been shown to contain various Ags and stimulate multiple immune pathways (Belkaid and Harrison, 2017), our result suggests that some commensal bacteria express TI-2 Ag-like repetitive structures that elicit IgG3 production.

source: Translocation of a gut pathobiont to the liver and other systemic tissues causes a lupus-like disease in genetically autoimmune-prone mice owing to induction of a systemic type I interferon response and autoantibody production (Manfredo Vieira et al., 2018).
